lens.name: Execute Period-End and Continuous Close
lens.description: Runs the period-end close from sub-ledger cutoff through journal posting, reconciliation, flux review and certification. More of it now runs continuously, with agents monitoring it.

industry.retail: High-volume, multi-location retailers must reconcile thousands of daily point-of-sale settlement batches, gift card/loyalty liabilities, and inventory-in-transit accruals before the books can close, making automated POS-to-GL matching and store-level cutoff discipline critical to a fast close.
industry.tech: Technology companies with multi-element subscription arrangements must true up deferred revenue waterfalls, stock-based compensation expense, and R&D capitalization judgments each period, so the close calendar typically embeds an extra revenue-recognition sub-close before consolidation.
industry.insurance: Insurer close cycles include actuarial reserve (loss and loss-adjustment-expense) estimation and reinsurance recoverable reconciliation alongside the standard GL close, and increasingly run statutory (SAP) and GAAP books in parallel.
industry.hotel: For a hotel company, this means closing the books property by property against the Uniform System of Accounts for the Lodging Industry (USALI), consolidating room revenue, F&B, and departmental results into portfolio-level close.
industry.manufacturing: For a manufacturer, close involves reconciling standard-cost variances, WIP inventory valuation, and cost-of-goods-sold from the plant's cost-accounting system alongside the standard journal-entry and reconciliation cycle.
industry.banking: For a bank, this means closing the books across interest income/expense accruals, loan-loss provisioning (CECL/IFRS 9), and trading-book valuations, with reconciliation and certification standards shaped by prudential reporting deadlines.

country.PH: Philippine entities must align close timing with BIR's monthly/quarterly VAT (2550M/2550Q) and withholding tax (1601-EQ) filing deadlines, and journal entries affecting revenue must reconcile to BIR-accredited Computerized Accounting System (CAS) records to avoid discrepancies at audit.
country.US: US public and many private companies operate the close under SOX Section 404 ICFR requirements, so every close task (reconciliation, JE approval, flux review) must carry documented evidence, segregation of duties, and preparer/reviewer sign-off retained for external auditor testing.
country.SG: Singapore entities close against Singapore Financial Reporting Standards (SFRS(I)) and must be audit-ready for ACRA's annual return, and where GST-registered, reconcile output/input tax to the F5 return filed with IRAS within one month of the accounting period end.

kpis: Number of late/manual adjusting entries post-close

lens.name: Manage Receipt, Invoice Matching, and Payment
lens.description: Receives goods and services, matches supplier invoices to the purchase order and receipt, resolves exceptions and pays suppliers on time, within controls. Agents increasingly handle the matching and exceptions.

industry.retail: High-volume merchandise vendor invoicing requires automated matching tolerant of retail-specific variances (quantity shortages, vendor chargebacks, promotional allowances deducted at payment), making exception-handling rules the single biggest driver of touchless-match rates.
industry.tech: Tech companies process a large share of non-PO/recurring SaaS invoices (subscriptions billed outside formal procurement), so invoice-to-pay automation must handle both traditional three-way match and lighter-weight recurring-vendor workflows with strong duplicate-payment detection.
industry.insurance: Invoice-to-pay for an insurer processes high-value technology and data-licensing invoices (policy administration, actuarial, catastrophe-modeling platforms) alongside routine claims-vendor and facilities spend.
industry.hotel: For a hotel company, this means matching deliveries of perishable F&B goods and supplies against purchase orders at the property receiving dock, resolving exceptions quickly given spoilage risk, and paying suppliers on time.
industry.manufacturing: For a manufacturer, this matches supplier invoices against PO and goods-receipt records at the plant receiving dock, with particular attention to quantity and quality discrepancies before releasing payment.
industry.banking: For a bank, this core invoice-to-pay flow operates alongside strict segregation-of-duties controls, since procurement payment processes sit under the same operational-risk and fraud-control scrutiny regulators apply to the bank's customer-facing payment rails.

country.PH: Supplier invoices received must be validated as BIR-compliant (proper OR/sales invoice format, TIN, VAT breakdown) to support input VAT claims, and withholding tax must be correctly computed and remitted (BIR Form 1601-EQ) at the time of payment, generating a BIR Form 2307 certificate to the supplier.
country.US: 1099 reporting obligations require capturing supplier TIN/W-9 data at onboarding so payments to US vendors are correctly reported to the IRS; SOX treats the three-way match and payment approval as key controls preventing unauthorized disbursement.
country.SG: GST input tax claims require the underlying tax invoice to meet IRAS format requirements, and companies are increasingly expected to receive supplier invoices via InvoiceNow (PEPPOL) for straight-through GST-compliant processing.

lens.name: Administer payroll
lens.description: Runs payroll end to end. Keeps pay master data current, calculates and pays salaries, and remits statutory contributions and taxes on time.

industry.retail: Retail payroll must process large volumes of hourly, shift-differential, and overtime pay across many locations on tight biweekly/weekly cycles, with high sensitivity to timekeeping-system accuracy given thin margins and wage-and-hour litigation risk.
industry.tech: Tech payroll must handle complex compensation elements — equity vesting events, sign-on/relocation bonuses, multi-state or multi-country remote-worker tax withholding — often through a global payroll aggregator given distributed workforces.
industry.insurance: Insurer payroll must administer producer/agent commission and contingent-commission payments alongside standard employee pay, and accurately track licensed-role compensation for state regulatory reporting.
industry.hotel: For a hotel company, this means running payroll across many properties with complex hourly, overtime, tip-pooling, and service-charge distribution rules, and remitting statutory contributions per local jurisdiction.
industry.manufacturing: For a manufacturer, payroll must handle multi-shift schedules, overtime, and union pay-rate rules alongside standard salaried payroll, remitting statutory contributions accurately across plant locations.
industry.banking: For a bank, payroll runs like any large enterprise's, though pay for regulated roles is often subject to additional deferral or clawback provisions tied to risk and compliance outcomes.

country.PH: Payroll must correctly compute and remit employee and employer shares to SSS, PhilHealth, and Pag-IBIG monthly, withhold income tax per the BIR withholding tax table (filing/remitting via BIR Form 1601-C monthly, with Form 2316 issued annually to each employee), and compute holiday pay, night-shift differential, and overtime per Labor Code formulas.
country.US: Payroll must comply with FLSA overtime rules (1.5x for non-exempt hours over 40/week, with some states requiring daily overtime), withhold and remit federal/state/local taxes and FICA, and issue Form W-2 annually; multi-state remote employees create nexus and withholding complexity.
country.SG: Payroll must compute mandatory CPF (Central Provident Fund) contributions for Singapore citizens/PRs on a graduated rate table by age band, and must submit annual IR8A income data to IRAS for tax filing via the Auto-Inclusion Scheme.

lens.name: Manage Customer Service Operations & Contact Center
lens.description: Operate the contact center and service channels that receive, triage, and route customer inquiries across voice, chat, email, and self-service.

industry.retail: Retail contact centers handle a mix of order status, returns, and loyalty inquiries with heavy seasonal volume spikes (holiday, sale events) requiring flexible surge staffing and in-store/digital handoff.
industry.tech: SaaS companies operate tiered technical support (L1 self-serve/community, L2 product support, L3 engineering escalation) with support entitlements gated by subscription plan (e.g., Basic vs. Premier support).
industry.insurance: Insurer contact centers handle policy service, billing, and first-notice-of-loss (FNOL) claims reporting, with catastrophe events driving extreme volume spikes that require surge staffing and overflow claims-intake capacity.
industry.hotel: For a hotel company, this means operating the central reservations contact center and guest-service channels that handle booking changes, loyalty inquiries, and complaints across voice, chat, and email, working in tandem with front-desk teams at each property.
industry.manufacturing: For a manufacturer, this operates the technical support and order-status contact center that fields inquiries from distributors and industrial end customers, often requiring product-specific technical knowledge rather than general service scripts.
industry.banking: For a bank, this means operating the contact center and digital-servicing channels handling account inquiries, card disputes, and fraud alerts, staffed and scripted to meet regulatory error-resolution and complaint-handling timelines.

country.PH: Contact centers operating in the Philippines (a major BPO hub) must comply with DOLE labor standards for shift/night differential pay and the NPC Data Privacy Act for handling caller PII.
country.US: Call recording for quality/training requires two-party consent compliance in certain states (e.g., California); accessibility of self-service channels should align with ADA-related digital accessibility expectations.
country.SG: Outbound service calls must screen against the PDPA Do Not Call Registry where marketing is involved; call recording requires PDPA-compliant consent notice.
